verdict.rationale: Honeybadger ships user-configurable rules that run unattended in the background. Alarms evaluate a BadgerQL query against a threshold and fire alerts, anomaly detection watches error volume against a learned baseline, open errors auto-resolve when a deploy is recorded, and uptime checks run on a schedule. These are fixed monitoring and alerting rules, though, not general-purpose or agent-driven automations; the MCP server only lets an assistant query data interactively. Missing for 10: user-defined multi-step automation workflows, autonomous agent actions that run without a prompt (e.g. auto-triage or auto-fix), scheduled custom jobs beyond alerts, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
